columns.name: Function
columns.desc: The nonlinearity in the feed-forward block (or after each convolution). GLU variants (GeGLU, SwiGLU) multiply two projections, so they use three matrices instead of two.

columns.name: FFN width
columns.desc: Hidden width of the feed-forward block divided by the model width d. For GLU variants the width of one of the two parallel projections. Sorts by the ratio.

columns.name: Type
columns.desc: Which normalisation layer: local response normalisation (LRN), BatchNorm, LayerNorm, or RMSNorm (no mean subtraction, no bias).

columns.name: Placement
columns.desc: Post-LN normalises after the residual add; pre-LN normalises the input of each sub-block; OLMo 2 normalises the output of the branch before the add; Gemma does both.

columns.name: Epsilon
columns.desc: The constant added inside the square root. Sorts by value.

columns.name: Scheme
columns.desc: How weights are drawn before step one.

columns.name: Std
columns.desc: Standard deviation of the base weight distribution, where one number describes it. Sorts by value.

columns.name: Type
columns.desc: SGD with momentum, Adam, Adam with decoupled weight decay (AdamW), Adafactor, or Muon.

columns.name: Betas or momentum
columns.desc: Adam beta1 and beta2, or the SGD momentum. Sorts by beta2 (or momentum).

columns.name: Epsilon
columns.desc: Adam's epsilon in the denominator. Sorts by value.

columns.name: Peak
columns.desc: Maximum learning rate of the main pretraining run. Not comparable across optimisers or batch sizes; shown for the record. Sorts by value.

columns.name: Warmup
columns.desc: How the learning rate starts.

columns.name: Decay shape
columns.desc: Step drops, inverse square root, linear, cosine, or warmup-stable-decay (WSD).

columns.name: Final
columns.desc: Final learning rate as a percentage of the peak. Sorts by value.

columns.name: Weight decay
columns.desc: Coefficient and whether it is coupled (added to the gradient, L2) or decoupled (applied to the weights directly, AdamW). Sorts by value.

columns.name: Dropout
columns.desc: Dropout probability during pretraining. Sorts by value.

columns.name: Grad clipping
columns.desc: Global gradient-norm clipping threshold. Sorts by value.

columns.name: Loss tweaks
columns.desc: Anything added to plain cross-entropy: label smoothing, z-loss, auxiliary balance or multi-token losses, distillation targets, a learned temperature.

columns.name: Batch size
columns.desc: Global batch in examples or tokens. Sorts by tokens where tokens apply, else by examples.

columns.name: Precision
columns.desc: Number formats used for training compute and for the master weights.

report.title: ImageNet Classification with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks

act.note: Section 3.1: a 4-layer convnet with ReLUs reached 25% training error on CIFAR-10 six times faster than with tanh.

ffn.note: The two fully connected layers are 4096 wide, but there is no residual FFN block to compare.

norm.q: we used k = 2, n = 5, alpha = 10^-4, and beta = 0.75
norm.note: Applied after the ReLU in the first two convolutional layers. It reduced top-1 error by 1.4%. BatchNorm did not exist yet.

neps.note: LRN adds k = 2 to the sum of squares before raising it to beta = 0.75; it plays the role epsilon plays in later norms, at a far larger value.

init.q: zero-mean Gaussian distribution with standard deviation 0.01
init.note: Biases of conv layers 2, 4, 5 and the hidden FC layers set to 1 so the ReLUs start with positive inputs; others 0.

lr.q: The learning rate was initialized at 0.01

warm.note: No warmup: the rate started at 0.01.

sched.q: divide the learning rate by 10 when the validation error rate stopped improving
sched.note: Adjusted by hand, three times, over about 90 epochs.

fin.note: Reduced three times prior to termination.

wd.q: v := 0.9 v - 0.0005 eps w - eps dL/dw
wd.note: The update rule puts the decay inside the momentum buffer, scaled by the learning rate: classic L2. The paper adds that it "reduces the model's training error", so it is not merely a regulariser.

drop.note: Without dropout the network overfit substantially; dropout roughly doubled the iterations to converge.

loss.note: The paper describes no label smoothing or other term; data augmentation (crops, flips, PCA colour noise) carried the regularisation.

prec.note: Two GTX 580 3GB GPUs, five to six days. The paper does not name a number format; the GTX 580 had no fast half precision.

corrections.claim: AdamW became the default with the LLMs of 2020 to 2023
corrections.primary: GPT (June 2018) already used Adam with "a modified version of L2 regularization" citing Loshchilov and Hutter, and BERT's released optimiser (October 2018) decays weights outside Adam's moments, though BERT's paper calls it "L2 weight decay".

corrections.claim: Learning-rate warmup was introduced by the Transformer
corrections.primary: ResNet (December 2015) trained its 110-layer CIFAR-10 net at 0.01 until training error fell below 80% (about 400 iterations), then switched to 0.1.
Mesh TensorFlow, the code T5 trained with in 2019, defaults to z_loss = 1e-4 (unconfirmed whether T5's runs kept it; the paper is silent). OLMo 2 cites PaLM, Chameleon and Wortsman et al. for it.

corrections.claim: A model's config.json tells you how it was initialised
corrections.primary: DeepSeek-V3's report says every parameter was drawn with std 0.006; its config.json says initializer_range 0.02. The config describes loading the checkpoint, not the run.
Only for ungated FFNs, and not always then: T5-11B uses 65,536 / 1,024 = 64x; SwiGLU models use 2.7x to 5.4x; Gemma 3 runs a gated FFN at 4x, which is 1.5 times the parameters of a plain 4x block.

corrections.claim: Llama 3 decays its learning rate to 10% of the peak
corrections.primary: The 405B decays by cosine to 8e-7, 1% of its 8e-5 peak, then linearly to 0 over the last 40M tokens. The 10% figure belongs to the scaling-law runs.
The report's phrase "a batch size of 8M sequences of 8,192 tokens" would be 65.5 billion tokens per step, 8,192 times too many; it means 8M tokens, the 4M batch doubled.
The paper's words say "exponentially decays"; its formula, 1/sqrt(max(n, 10^4)), is an inverse square root, which at 1M steps is still 10% of the peak.
OLMo 2 normalises the output of each attention and MLP branch before adding it to the residual stream; the stream itself is never normalised inside a block.

corrections.claim: Gemma 3 soft-caps its logits like Gemma 2
corrections.primary: Gemma 3 replaced soft-capping with QK-norm; final_logit_softcapping and attn_logit_softcapping are unset in its config.

corrections.claim: SmolLM3 trains with z-loss (reading its config)
corrections.primary: The config sets z_loss_coefficient 1e-5 but z_loss_enabled false.
BERT's released AdamWeightDecayOptimizer has decoupled decay, epsilon 1e-6 and no bias correction of m and v.

corrections.claim: Adam's epsilon is a harmless constant
corrections.primary: OLMo 2 lowered it from 1e-5 (Llama 2's value) to 1e-8 and saw a lower, steadier gradient norm early in training and faster loss improvement.
